Actions.Label: Have a proper chat
Say: Rain makes the basement window look like an aquarium. I can sit there for an hour and pretend the world is somewhere else.
Sam sent me a voice memo of a song idea. It was mostly traffic noise and one very confident wrong note.
Robin asked if I wanted to help with a shelf. I said maybe. She put the wood aside anyway.
I like the quiet hours in the morning, before the town starts deciding what it needs from everybody.
Someone left a tiny plastic frog on my desk. I know it was Sam. I haven't moved it.
Programming is mostly being wrong in increasingly specific ways until the machine agrees to stop complaining.
I've been riding out to the lake at night. Not to think. Just to hear something that isn't a fan spinning.
Maru says I should open the curtains more often. I told her the curtains have done nothing to deserve that.
I started a new game. It has six endings and none of them involve paying rent. Excellent design.
Alex asked if I wanted to join a game outside. I said no, then spent the afternoon watching from the porch.
I don't hate family dinners. I hate being asked what I'm doing with my life between the potatoes and dessert.
Sam has a talent for turning a normal afternoon into a story that takes three days to explain.
I keep a list of things I might build. Most are apps. One is a very bad idea for a weather machine.
The old motorcycle needs work. I know. I can hear the chain complaining from the shed.
Leah brought a carving over to show Robin. I liked it more than I expected. Didn't say that quickly enough.
I found a folder of old code. Half of it is useless. The other half is somehow worse.
I don't mind being alone. I mind when people decide that being alone means I'm waiting to be rescued.
There's a town event next week. I might go. Don't make it weird if you see me there.
Sam says I'm the only person who can make a compliment sound like a bug report. She's probably right.
The basement gets cold in winter. I keep a blanket behind the chair. No, you can't have it. ...Fine, maybe.
I've been taking more walks. I don't tell anybody where I'm going because I don't always know until I get there.
Robin's been talking about Leah's cottage. She sounds less tense when she says the word 'home'.
I like the sound of the arcade when nobody is playing. Machines humming, lights clicking. It's almost peaceful.
Some people write in journals. I save screenshots. Same idea, less handwriting.
You're easier to talk to than most people. Don't look pleased. It's a very small compliment.

Steps.Narrate: A folded note is tucked beneath the keyboard in Sebastian's basement room. She taps it once, then turns the screen off.

Steps.Say: I wrote this last night. Not code. Actual sentences. Don't make a face.
It's about the house. Not one thing, exactly. Just how everybody seems to have a place and a reason to be in it.
Robin's in the shop, Maru has her projects, Demetrius has a paper for everything. I have the basement and a window that sticks.
I don't want somebody to tell me I should be grateful. I am. I also want a room that doesn't feel like the spare part of a family.
Can you read it? Not for grammar. I know the grammar is bad. Just tell me whether it sounds like me.
Honest is good. I can work with honest. Maybe I'll leave the note where I can find it instead of deleting it.

Options.Label: Write what you wish you could say to them.

Steps.Say: That's the problem. I can write it. Saying it while someone's looking at me is a separate skill.

Options.Label: You deserve a space of your own.

Steps.Say: Yeah. I think I want to believe that without having to argue for it first.
I'm going to keep the note. That's all for today. And don't tell Sam I wrote something sincere. She'll make it a song.

Actions.Label: A ride past the lights
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch1_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 4, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 6, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: Sebastian is checking the motorcycle chain outside. A helmet rests on the seat beside a second one.

Steps.Say: I was going to ride to the beach. Then I thought it might be better not to go alone. Don't read into the second helmet.
The road is different at night. You see the windows lit up and imagine what everybody's doing. Most of the time it's probably dishes.
I keep thinking about leaving. Not because I hate this place. Because I want to know whether I could choose somewhere else and still come back.
Sam says the city would suit me. She also says every city has a pizza place and I should choose based on that.
I don't want to make a dramatic exit. I just want to take a road because I decided to.

Options.Label: The beach. No plan beyond that.

Steps.Say: Good. We can turn around whenever. I like a trip with an exit that doesn't need explaining.
All right. Past the saloon, the bridge, the dark windows. I want to see the place without having to talk about it.

Options.Label: Stay here and fix the chain.

Steps.Say: Practical. Annoyingly practical. ...Fine. Help me hold the wheel steady.
Thanks. I didn't need an audience. Just somebody who wouldn't turn a ride into a referendum on my future.

Actions.Label: The room with two windows
Actions.Conditions: Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch2_{{NpcName}}, PLAYER_HEARTS Current {{NpcName}} 6, Fouky.CharacterInteract_COUNTER Talks_{{NpcName}} 10, !Fouky.CharacterInteract_HAS_FLAG Ch3_{{NpcName}}

Steps.Narrate: A sketch lies on the table. It shows a small room with two windows, shelves, and a desk facing the trees.

Steps.Say: I drew this after the ride. Not a house. Not a whole new life. Just a room where the light comes in from both sides.
I've been saving money. Not enough yet, but enough to stop pretending it's only an idea.
Robin offered to look at the measurements. Leah said she'd help me find a chair. Sam already named the room something ridiculous.
Maybe I stay here another year. Maybe I go. I don't think the answer has to be decided by how annoyed I am on a Tuesday.
I wanted you to see it because you're part of the reason I stopped treating the future like a thing that happens to other people.

Options.Label: It looks like somewhere you'd want to be.

Steps.Say: That's the point. I want to walk into a room and not feel like I'm borrowing it.

Options.Label: Build it here, then decide later.

Steps.Say: I like that. Build first. The road can wait until I know what I'm carrying.

Options.Label: Take the sketch with you wherever you go.

Steps.Say: Yeah. I'll fold it carefully. Probably put it in the same drawer as the note. That's a pattern, I guess.
Keep the other copy. If I lose mine, I know who to ask. It's not sentimental. It's document redundancy.
